source_metadata.exact_title: Prediction of structural glaucoma progression from baseline fundus photographs using deep learning: a retrospective multicentre study
source_metadata.source_scope_note: The retrieved PDF contains the 12-page main article. The repeatedly cited online appendix was not embedded in the retrieved PDF and was therefore not inspected.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to develop and externally validate G-PROG, a deep learning model that predicts 2–5-year structural glaucoma progression from a single baseline colour fundus photograph.
Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older at baseline.

population.label: Adults considered for inclusion
inclusion_criteria: Age 18 years or older at baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: Eye inclusion required at least three visits with colour fundus photographs for a given eye.

population.label: Eyes considered for inclusion
inclusion_criteria: At least three visits with colour fundus photographs for the eye

atoms.canonical_statement: The six-site study included 13,913 patients and 128,021 eye-years of follow-up across glaucoma departments in Belgium, Finland, Germany, and China.
The Leuven cohort included 3,519 participants, 6,499 eyes, 31,929 visits, and 56,371 fundus photographs.

atoms.canonical_statement: G-PROG was trained and internally validated using UZ Leuven data, while Brussels, Liège, Tampere, Mainz, and Hangzhou datasets were reserved as external test sets.
Eligible fundus photographs were transformed to 30-degree disc-centred images before analysis.
G-RISK is a previously validated regression convolutional neural network trained on expert-estimated vertical cup-to-disc ratio; larger G-RISK values indicate greater glaucomatous optic nerve damage.
The study defined structural glaucoma progression using the within-eye linear-regression slope of longitudinal G-RISK predictions, termed the G-RISK slope.

outcome.definition: Within-eye linear-regression slope of G-RISK predictions over time

atoms.canonical_statement: A fixed baseline G-RISK threshold of 0.6 was used in selected analyses to identify eyes with a high likelihood of established glaucomatous optic nerve damage.

Three auxiliary convolutional neural networks screened eligible photographs for optic-disc presence, image quality, and consistent eye laterality; only photographs passing these checks were retained and no imputation was used.
G-PROG used an EfficientNet-B0 encoder and was trained to regress the G-RISK slope from a baseline colour fundus photograph.

exposures.details: EfficientNet-B0 regression model using a baseline CFP

outcome.definition: Estimated structural glaucoma progression rate over the next 2–5 years

atoms.canonical_statement: Twenty G-PROG configurations were trained with different interval-selection and inclusion criteria to study the effects of follow-up structure and image constraints.
UZ Leuven data were split 60%/20%/20% into training, validation, and test sets at the patient level to prevent leakage across splits.

For external testing, the eight configurations with positive R2 and the smallest discrepancies between R2 and explained variance score in internal validation were selected and combined by an unweighted mean; no recalibration or post-hoc adjustment was performed.
G-PROG discrimination was evaluated by AUC over G-RISK slope thresholds from 0 to 0.075 in increments of 0.001, with 95% confidence intervals computed using DeLong’s method.

outcome.measurement_method: ROC AUC over G-RISK slope thresholds

atoms.canonical_statement: Additional regression metrics included R2, explained variance score, Pearson correlation, mean absolute error, and improvement in mean absolute error from baseline.

Performance was stratified by baseline visual-field mean deviation into early, moderate, and advanced glaucoma, but formal evaluation across age, sex, ethnicity, or other sociodemographic subgroups and fairness metrics was not performed.
The G-RISK slope was compared with established functional and structural progression biomarkers using visual-field mean deviation slope and average retinal nerve fibre layer slope.

concept.text: MD slope and average RNFL slope
Agreement with established glaucoma progression biomarkers

atoms.canonical_statement: Explainability analysis averaged saliency maps after optic-disc recentering using the single configuration with the best R2 on internal validation.
The analysis included 161,827 fundus images.
The analysis included 127,962 clinical visits.
Across the extracted data, 28,704 progression intervals were evaluated, including 17,028 intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6.
Eighteen of 20 G-PROG configurations achieved AUC values significantly above 0.5 in validation sets with at least five visits.
In the UZ Leuven validation data with at least five visits, maximum AUC across all intervals was 0.98 (95% CI 0.97–1.00).

population.label: UZ Leuven validation intervals with at least five visits

atoms.canonical_statement: In the UZ Leuven validation data restricted to intervals with baseline G-RISK above 0.6 and at least five visits, maximum AUC was 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.98).

population.label: UZ Leuven validation glaucomatous intervals with at least five visits

atoms.canonical_statement: In the internal UZ Leuven test set, maximum AUC across all intervals was 0.91 (95% CI 0.83–0.99) at a G-RISK slope threshold of 0.036 per year.
In the internal UZ Leuven test set restricted to baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.96 (95% CI 0.88–1.00) at a G-RISK slope threshold of 0.030 per year.

population.label: UZ Leuven internal test glaucomatous intervals

atoms.canonical_statement: Across configurations with at least five visits, R2 ranged from -0.59 to 0.11 and was positive in 9 of 20 experiments.

population.label: G-PROG experiments with at least five visits

atoms.canonical_statement: Across configurations, explained variance score ranged from -0.06 to 0.11.
Pearson correlation between predicted and ground-truth G-RISK slopes was 0.42 in validation data.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pearson correlation between predicted and ground-truth G-RISK slopes was 0.39 in internal test data.

atoms.canonical_statement: In Brussels external testing, maximum AUC was 0.79 (95% CI 0.71–0.88) across all intervals.
In Brussels intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.73 (95% CI 0.66–0.80).
In Liège external testing, maximum AUC was 0.78 (95% CI 0.70–0.86) across all intervals.
In Liège intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.76 (95% CI 0.68–0.85).
In Tampere external testing, maximum AUC was 0.62 (95% CI 0.57–0.66) across all intervals.
In Tampere intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.74 (95% CI 0.66–0.82).
In Mainz external testing, maximum AUC was 0.81 (95% CI 0.68–0.93) across all intervals.
In Mainz intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.63–0.88).
In the Hangzhou GRAPE external dataset, maximum AUC was 0.86 (95% CI 0.52–1.00) across all intervals.
In Hangzhou GRAPE intervals with baseline G-RISK at least 0.6, maximum AUC was 0.77 (95% CI 0.50–1.00).
For discrimination of functional progression defined by visual-field MD slope, G-RISK slope achieved maximum AUC values from 0.67 to 0.82 across analysed thresholds and strata.

atoms.canonical_statement: Average saliency maps consistently concentrated most strongly on the optic disc across internal and external datasets, with weaker recurrent saliency inferior to the disc.
External-site performance varied by cohort and follow-up density, with Tampere showing lower all-interval discrimination than several other external datasets.
The authors concluded that G-PROG can predict individualised 2–5-year structural glaucoma progression from a single baseline colour fundus photograph across multiple external cohorts.
The authors proposed that G-PROG could improve glaucoma risk stratification at diagnosis and help prioritise closer monitoring for patients at higher predicted progression risk.
The authors stated that prospective evaluation is needed before establishing G-PROG’s clinical utility.
The authors recommended future validation in untreated cohorts or a prospective multimodal study with structural and functional testing at regular intervals.
Because G-RISK is bounded above at 1, the derived G-RISK slope could exhibit a ceiling effect in advanced disease.
Intervals with more visits tended to show higher AUC values, creating potential selection bias from better trend estimation or closer monitoring of higher-risk patients.
The baseline G-RISK threshold of 0.6 and progression-slope thresholds may require population-specific refinement.

The G-RISK slope ground truth was derived from eyes under active management, so geographically varying treatment practices can influence observed progression and the reference standard used to evaluate G-PROG.
Ethnicity was unavailable in participating electronic health records, limiting assessment of performance across ethnic groups.
Formal sociodemographic subgroup evaluation and fairness metrics were not performed.
The study reported funding from multiple Singaporean, Finnish, Belgian, and glaucoma-research organizations.
The authors stated that funders had no role in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, manuscript writing, or the decision to submit.

The paper disclosed that G-RISK had been transferred to Mona.health; Ingeborg Stalmans was a cofounder, shareholder, and consultant, and Ruben Hemelings was entitled to stock options and had received consultancy fees from Mona.health.
The GRAPE dataset is publicly available, while several other centre datasets require collaboration agreements, approvals, or on-site/controlled access.
The study code for estimating structural glaucoma progression is available in a public G-PROG repository; trained models are available upon academically reasonable request.

extraction_limitations: The online appendix cited throughout the article was not included in the retrieved 12-page PDF; appendix-only model configuration details, software specifics, additional ROC curves, subgroup tables, and sensitivity analyses were not atomized.
Atoms are anchored to PDF page and section/figure/table locators; paragraph/sentence indices were not added because the two-column PDF text extraction does not preserve stable paragraph numbering.
No external sources were used to fill missing study details or to reinterpret reported results.
